persons.name: Amelia (ex-husband)
persons.harm: Her husband, addicted to opiates and later methamphetamine, emotionally neglected and verbally abused her, then after she filed for divorce stalked her phone, harassed and threatened her (including a gun-store location and 'go quietly' text), pushed her, threw a toy at her face, took their son for a $5,000 ransom, and finally broke in and set their house on fire.

quotes.quote: And one of the questions on the sheet was, are you a victim of domestic violence? And I checked no.

contacts.when: after the chainsaw incident, many night-time calls (8-10 visits)
contacts.what_was_asked: protection from nightly harassment and threats
contacts.what_institution_did: Came to the house repeatedly but said they could do nothing unless he physically assaulted her.
contacts.quote: The police would come and they would say until he physically assaults you, there's nothing we can do.
contacts.what_happened_next: Harassment continued and escalated.

contacts.what_was_asked: cut his access to her phone account
contacts.what_institution_did: Security worked to shut his line off but could not stop him reactivating it.
contacts.quote: they said this guy is good. We don't know how he's getting through all these walls, we keep shutting his phone off and he keeps turning it back on and we don't know how he's doing it.
contacts.what_happened_next: He kept tracking her phone.

contacts.when: after he pushed her and threw a toy at her face
contacts.what_institution_did: Said it sounded like assault but without visible marks they could do nothing.
contacts.quote: I called the police and told them what happened. They said it sounds like assault but we don't see any physical marks so we can't do anything.
contacts.what_happened_next: No action; she kept documenting.

contacts.what_was_asked: protection after a perceived death threat
contacts.what_institution_did: Held him outside so she could collect her things; looking at the 'shrine' said crazy is not illegal and they could do nothing.
contacts.quote: And he looks at it and I said, this is not normal. And he said, oh, it's definitely crazy, but crazy is not illegal. We can't do anything.
contacts.what_happened_next: She left to stay with a friend.
contacts.notes: Earlier at 16:32: 'we'll hold him outside and you go in and you get your things.'

contacts.institution: local police called by her workplace security
contacts.when: morning he came to her workplace
contacts.what_institution_did: Police spoke with him and with her; no step shown.
contacts.quote: And then the police come in and start talking to me about what's going on. And I fill them in on the chaos that our life has become.
contacts.what_happened_next: He went to the daycare and took their son.

contacts.what_was_asked: call her if he showed up
contacts.what_institution_did: Director was about to call her when he arrived; could not stop him taking the child.
contacts.quote: the director of the daycare has the phone in her handage that I was just about to call you.
contacts.what_happened_next: He took their oldest son.
contacts.notes: She had told them: 'I know you can't keep him from picking up our boys, but just call me'.

contacts.when: same day, during the ransom abduction
contacts.what_institution_did: Dispatched a helicopter and told her to get a restraining order.
contacts.quote: I told that to the police and they dispatched a helicopter to try to find the car.
contacts.what_happened_next: Officer: 'you need to go now to the courthouse and get a restraining order.' The father brought the boy back himself at midnight.

contacts.what_institution_did: Clerk recognised it as domestic violence; judge granted an order requiring him to leave the house.
contacts.quote: and I said it was granted. He's like, yeah, it was granted. Basically saying he has to leave the house immediately.
contacts.what_happened_next: Order could not take effect until served.
contacts.notes: Clerk: 'that's domestic violence' (24:48). Built on photos and texts collected for the divorce.

contacts.what_was_asked: help; she had an unserved order and was scared
contacts.what_institution_did: Sheriffs served the order immediately and removed him, warning he would go to jail if he returned.
contacts.quote: I said, I thought you guys didn't do that. They're like, no, we'll do it right now.
contacts.what_happened_next: He was removed; later arrested for DUI (meth).

contacts.what_institution_did: Judge kept him out of the home but allowed visitation monitored by his mother; she then dropped the order with stipulations.
contacts.quote: The judge basically said that he still had to stay away from the home and he was still not allowed in our residence,
contacts.what_happened_next: Three days later he broke in and set the house on fire.

contacts.institution: police, SWAT team, hostage negotiator and fire department
contacts.what_institution_did: Six-hour standoff; he surrendered and was taken away.
contacts.quote: A few hours later, finally he surrendered. The SWAT team went inside and brought him out.
contacts.what_happened_next: He was taken to hospital then jail.
contacts.notes: Neighbours (third parties) also called 911.

contacts.what_institution_did: Issued an emergency protective order; he was jailed; she was registered for custody-change alerts.
contacts.quote: [perpetrator] is on his way to jail. I was told because I got an emergency protective order from the sheriffs that night.
contacts.what_happened_next: He was later released on bail; the alert system notified her.

contacts.what_institution_did: Took her and the boys in, escorted by police; she left after two days because of the conditions.
contacts.quote: So I packed up the room and we went to a women's shelter. You follow the police car and they take you to the women's shelter.
contacts.what_happened_next: She left: 'It was awful ... not the environment that I wanted my boys in.'

contacts.what_was_asked: (his former employer requested a threat assessment)
contacts.what_institution_did: Added patrols around her hotel.
contacts.quote: the detective said, we're going to do some extra patrols around the hotel you're staying in to make sure that you're safe. It gave me a little bit of solace.
contacts.what_happened_next: Criminal case proceeded.

contacts.what_institution_did: Housed them, then covered 100% of the loss because she had the restraining order; denied his claims.
contacts.quote: They said it's not normal that they would cover an arson by someone that owned the home, but because I had the restraining order and because I did everything to get him out of the house and this was not my doing, that they would cover me a hundred percent.
contacts.what_happened_next: They moved into a house paid for by the insurer.

contacts.what_institution_did: Ordered a 730 evaluation and allowed visitation only when monitored by his parents.
contacts.quote: What was decided was that he could have monitored visitation by his parents, by his step-on and dad.
contacts.what_happened_next: Monitored visits went ahead.

contacts.when: a year and a half to two years after the arson
contacts.what_institution_did: Convicted him of felony arson, breaking and entering and vandalism; one year of pay-and-stay jail and three years' probation.
contacts.quote: Ultimately, he was convicted of felony arson, breaking an entering and vandalism for all of that. He received one year of jail time with eligibility for a pay and stay jail if he could afford it, which he could.
contacts.what_happened_next: She gave a victim impact statement; he served nights in jail for a year.
contacts.notes: She said: 'Quite honestly that felt so unfair at the time.' Conviction itself would be believed_and_acted; coded partly because of the sentence she describes as unfair.

contacts.when: after his parents took the boys out of the county
contacts.what_institution_did: Terminated visitation.
contacts.quote: So we called him into court and the judge terminated visitation.
contacts.what_happened_next: Boys did not see him during his incarceration.

contacts.when: at a hearing after the arson
contacts.what_institution_did: Judge said he questioned her judgment for dropping the first restraining order.
contacts.quote: The judge basically reprimanded me for dropping that first restraining order, and my house was burned down three days later.
contacts.what_happened_next: She said this stuck with her.
contacts.notes: Judge: 'I have a lot of respect for mom, but one thing that I don't is that she dropped the restraining order. I questioned mom's judgment.'

persons.outcome_quote: my life is blissfully predictable. I know what my house looks like when I open that door every day.
persons.decisive_work_quote: [perpetrator] is on his way to jail. I was told because I got an emergency protective order from the sheriffs that night.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: after police had been to the house 'like eight or 10 times'; the first effective order came the day of the abduction
persons.notes: The ex parte order and sheriff removal were effective at first, but she dropped the order after the hearing and he burned the house three days later. The harm ended with his arrest after the arson, followed by protective orders, supervised visitation and conviction, so coded protected. Witnesses: her mother listened by phone; a friend saw the texts. The ER visits in E1 were about his drug use, not harm to her, so they are not counted. Red Cross gift cards, the custody-change alert line and the DUI arrest are not separate contacts. He is now described as recovered and co-parenting.

persons.name: [unnamed] Amelia's oldest son
persons.harm: At three he was taken from daycare by his father, who was on drugs, driven unbuckled through red lights, and held for a $5,000 ransom; later exposed to the loss of the home.

contacts.what_was_asked: call his mother if the father came
contacts.what_institution_did: Director was calling his mother when the father arrived; could not legally stop the pickup.
contacts.quote: the director of the daycare has the phone in her handage that I was just about to call you.
contacts.what_happened_next: He was taken.

contacts.what_institution_did: Sent a helicopter; told his mother to get a restraining order.
contacts.quote: I told that to the police and they dispatched a helicopter to try to find the car.
contacts.what_happened_next: His father brought him home himself around midnight.

contacts.what_institution_did: Served the restraining order and removed the father from the home.
contacts.quote: I said, I thought you guys didn't do that. They're like, no, we'll do it right now.
contacts.what_happened_next: Father removed.

contacts.what_institution_did: Allowed only visitation monitored by the paternal grandparents.
contacts.quote: What was decided was that he could have monitored visitation by his parents, by his step-on and dad.
contacts.what_happened_next: Grandparents took the boys out of the county.

contacts.what_institution_did: Terminated visitation.
contacts.quote: So we called him into court and the judge terminated visitation.
contacts.what_happened_next: Later a slow step-up to every other weekend.

persons.outcome_quote: He remembers that day that [perpetrator] showed up at his daycare to take him and he still talks about it
persons.decisive_work_quote: So we called him into court and the judge terminated visitation.
persons.notes: The abduction itself ended when the father returned the boy, not through any institution. Court orders after that restricted access, so coded partly_protected. He now sees his father every other weekend after a step-up process. His younger brother is not given a separate record.

persons.name: Odessa
persons.harm: Her husband, a youth pastor, coerced her into long, painful sex that injured her nearly every time, began sex while she was asleep, guilt-tripped her when she refused, lied about pornography and an affair, and abandoned her while she was pregnant.

quotes.quote: Did you see this as sexual abuse at the time? No. I literally thought of it as my job.
It was never a thing that was encouraged to talk to other people at length about sex, especially in the church.

contacts.what_institution_did: Told her to refrain from sex for a while because of her injuries.
contacts.quote: there was a few times where I did get pretty decently injured and I was told by my doctor that I needed to reframe from having sex for a while.
contacts.what_happened_next: For a time this let her say no.
contacts.notes: It is unclear how much of the cause the doctor was told.

contacts.when: about six months pregnant, after he said he was leaving
contacts.what_institution_did: Staff asked repeatedly whether she was safe and offered to have him removed or call security; she declined, and they arranged therapy and medication.
contacts.quote: I had so many people asking me if I was safe, if I needed an out, if I needed him to leave, if I needed security to help.
contacts.what_happened_next: She went home and started individual therapy.
contacts.notes: 'They all believed me and they worked with me to get a therapist that I love and I got on some medications and they sent me home.' She told them she was fine.

contacts.when: couples counselling after the pornography disclosure
contacts.what_was_asked: help with their sex life and marriage
contacts.what_institution_did: Told her that to cure his addiction she had to become his 'new drug', always available to him sexually.
contacts.quote: She looked at me and said, Odessa, if you want to help him get through this addiction, you're going to have to become his new drug, his new addiction.
contacts.what_happened_next: She agreed out of fear of losing the marriage; her later therapist called it enabling her abuser.
contacts.notes: Coded as making her responsible for the harm. Her current therapist: 'your therapist was enabling your abuser.' Also endangered her.

persons.outcome_quote: And it's so disgusting that a person with a freaking license would enable that type of trauma and claim that it's my job
persons.notes: The harm ended when he left and the marriage broke up, not through any institution. She later used a lawyer for co-parenting and divorce agreements (no court response described). Present state: 'We tolerate each other ... We only interact at drop-offs' (E4 @ 50:52). The sister and friends are second witnesses. She re-read his eight-page letter on air (paraphrased in parts), hence document_read_on_air with low certainty. A previous emotionally abusive relationship (E3 @ 4:13) is only mentioned.

persons.name: Madison
persons.harm: A youth-group student whom the youth pastor groomed from 16 (late-night texts, a year-long Snapchat streak) and with whom he had a sexual affair once she was 18-19; she asked Odessa whether he guilt-tripped her about sex too.

contacts.when: while she was a minor in the youth group
contacts.what_institution_did: The lead pastor told him to have another adult in the car when driving girls home; the concern was framed around the student.
contacts.quote: Some of our other pastors or elders at our church are lead pastor even pulled [perpetrator] aside at one time and they were like, I really appreciate that you're willing to drive these kids home after youth group, but I think it would be really, really important for you to make sure that there's another person in the car whenever you are driving home a female specifically
contacts.what_happened_next: The closeness continued; they later had an affair.
contacts.notes: Odessa: 'It always seemed like everybody was expecting Madison to do something, but no one expected [perpetrator].' The church saw boundary concerns, not reported harm, so reached_institution is unclear.

persons.outcome_quote: After a few weeks, it came out that they were officially back together, Madison and [perpetrator].
persons.notes: Only told from Odessa's side. 'He met her when she was 16, was her youth pastor until she was 18' (E4 @ 37:11). Odessa: 'she is also a victim' (E4 @ 31:07). Another student and an elder knew of the affair.

persons.name: Natalia (partner met on dating app)
persons.harm: A long-distance partner filmed her having sex without consent, raged at her in her home, then after she ended it harassed her nonstop from spoofed and burner numbers (including imitating her friends' numbers), sent dozens of flower and food deliveries, and threatened to show up at her home.
persons.perpetrator_role: partner met on a queer dating app

quotes.quote: I was absolutely terrified because I still remember that line that his ID says that he's a woman. And because it says he's a woman that cops aren't going to give him the same amount of stress as if he was a bit.

It didn't feel good. It didn't feel good, especially black trans people because going to jail is such a horrible experience for them and it's so dehumanizing, but at the end of the day, it came down to the fact, is it going to be him or me?

contacts.what_was_asked: help; she did not know what to do
contacts.what_institution_did: Validated her and connected her to a local shelter and legal aid.
contacts.quote: This woman on the phone made me feel so seen and made me feel less like I have another statistic again. She connected me into the local shelter and she connected me to some type of legal aid.
contacts.what_happened_next: Shelter referred her to a legal fellow.

contacts.institution: local shelter and legal aid (legal fellow, supervised attorney)
contacts.what_institution_did: Prepared and filed an emergency restraining order with her; later represented her in court and refused a settlement.
contacts.quote: And so the shelter was able to connect me to someone who was a legal law ship fellow. We did the restraining order together and we filed an emergency restraining order.
contacts.what_happened_next: Order granted within five days.
contacts.notes: Representation: 'They were able to assist with legal advice and representing me in court' (40:50).

contacts.what_institution_did: Judge approved an emergency restraining order.
contacts.quote: Within about five days from calling the shelter to speaking to the fellow to getting the paperwork filed, the judge approved an emergency restraining order, but then I had to get it to him.
contacts.what_happened_next: She found his mother's address and he was served.

contacts.what_institution_did: Served the emergency order.
contacts.quote: So the sheriff served him with the emergency restraining order and they made court.
contacts.what_happened_next: Deliveries stopped; she felt she could sleep.

contacts.when: after a continuance requested by his lawyer
contacts.what_institution_did: Judge reviewed her screenshots, rejected his account, and granted a six-month protective order.
contacts.quote: and the judge didn't buy it. And I am grateful that the judge didn't buy it, but then I'm also not grateful because they only granted me a six month protection order against him.
contacts.what_happened_next: She has not heard from him since.
contacts.notes: 'Even though multiple people have multiple restraining orders against him, I only get a six month one.'

persons.outcome_quote: But I haven't heard from him since that last court case. And I am grateful.
persons.decisive_work_quote: We did the restraining order together and we filed an emergency restraining order.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: about five days after she first called the hotline/shelter
persons.notes: She also did the work herself: she found his court records (several DV restraining orders and a DV jail record), sent her evidence, and refused his lawyer's settlement so there would be a record. The secret sex recording was never separately pursued. Friends received spoofed calls (second witnesses).

persons.name: Natalia (earlier abusive ex-partner)
persons.harm: An earlier partner hit her and repeatedly kicked her out; she lived with him for years before fleeing at night, and she says he caused her PTSD.

contacts.what_institution_did: Provided therapy; nothing more is described.
contacts.quote: I had been through hell and back with [perpetrator]. I had gone to therapy and had gone to a trauma counselor and I had done all of these things
contacts.what_happened_next: She moved across the country.

persons.outcome_quote: I left [perpetrator] with whatever I could fit in my car and I drove in the middle of the night.
persons.notes: Told only in passing. 'the person who is responsible for my PTSD' (E6 @ 24:07); '[perpetrator] hit you' as quoted by the later partner (E6 @ 23:03). No police contact is mentioned. Her grandparents sheltered her.

persons.name: Ruksana (impersonation and hacking)
persons.harm: For about three years someone hijacked her email and Facebook: they cancelled her appointments, told her AA sponsees she had relapsed, sent threats in her name, and posted Arabic pro-Muslim Brotherhood content, isolating her and leading her family to suspect she had been radicalized.
persons.perpetrator_role: unidentified; suspects include online 'friends' who steered her to a married man she had an affair with, his wife, or others

quotes.quote: They had seen the emails and I couldn't necessarily defend myself because I was scared that maybe I did it, but it didn't help to have your own parents be suspicious of you.

contacts.when: when she discovered the Facebook posts
contacts.what_institution_did: Said whoever was doing this was watching her and advised her to leave the city.
contacts.quote: My therapist was like, you need to leave the city. You need to go home to stay with your family for a period of time.
contacts.what_happened_next: She went home to her parents.

contacts.when: after returning home, with her mother
contacts.what_was_asked: she half expected to turn herself in
contacts.what_institution_did: Told her she was not a terrorist but had been hacked; worked through IP addresses and emails with her.
contacts.quote: And as I started explaining my case to the detective, he was like, absolutely not. You're not a terrorist. Totally not. Your shit got hacked.
contacts.what_happened_next: He contacted everyone on her email list.
contacts.notes: He also mocked her: 'how did you believe this woman was in China and she was a shaman. Like, you're a grown woman.'

contacts.what_institution_did: Hard to reach; she had to prove she was not the poster.
contacts.quote: it was so hard when you try to write to Facebook and ask them to shut something down. It was such a fiasco to have to prove to yourself that you're not that person or that your account has been hacked.
contacts.what_happened_next: Someone was changing her password in real time.

contacts.when: after the posts came to light
contacts.what_was_asked: her parents wanted her checked for 'programming'
contacts.what_institution_did: She was made to see a sheikh to be 'deprogrammed'; his response is not described.
contacts.quote: They took me to the mosque. I had to talk to a shake to see if I had been programmed or see if he could deprogram me. It was a shit show.
contacts.what_happened_next: Her relationship with her parents was never repaired.

contacts.when: after IP addresses traced to Amsterdam, Nigeria and government addresses
contacts.what_institution_did: Stopped helping, told her to change her name, and said she was at fault for not protecting herself.
contacts.quote: He looked at me and he was like, you know what? I can't help you. He was done. He wasn't going to help me anymore. And he was like, listen, if I were you, I would change your name.
contacts.what_happened_next: No resolution; she changed her name and moved.
contacts.notes: Same passage: 'And then he said that I was the one at fault because I didn't protect myself.' He also dropped the case (did_nothing).

persons.outcome_quote: And then he said that I was the one at fault because I didn't protect myself.
persons.notes: 'So there was really no resolution' (36:22). Her cousin saw the posts and her sponsor showed her a fake email (second witnesses). The perpetrator was never identified.

persons.name: Ruksana (ex-boyfriend)
persons.harm: She lived with an abusive, 'super toxic' boyfriend whose behaviour got worse when she tried to get sober.
persons.outcome_quote: I had a boyfriend I was living with at the time, and it was like a super toxic relationship that got even more toxic when I tried to get sober. So I had to move out.
persons.notes: Only briefly told. Her CPTSD may stem 'from the abusive relationship I was in'. It is unclear whether she raised this harm in therapy. She left on her own. He was one of the theories for the later hacking.

persons.name: Sage
persons.harm: A Hinge date living under a false name (with hired actors posing as family) love-bombed her, slammed her into a wall and tried to force her toward sex while drunk, then tracked her phone and tried to break into her apartment three times while leaving notes.
persons.perpetrator_role: a man she dated from Hinge (con man using a false identity)

quotes.quote: I should have called the cops, but I didn't. I was like, you know what, this is just another one of those bad guys that you ran into.
I was scared to call the cops because cops are scary.

contacts.what_was_asked: act on the break-in and his note
contacts.what_institution_did: Did nothing.
contacts.quote: And so I reported that and the complex didn't do anything about it. They were like, okay, whatever.
contacts.what_happened_next: A second, more aggressive break-in attempt followed.

contacts.when: the morning after the second attempt
contacts.what_institution_did: Said they could do nothing and she should call the police.
contacts.quote: I told them I was going on and I'm crying and I have the note in my hand of what he sent me and they literally were like, we can't do anything for you. You just need to call the cops.
contacts.what_happened_next: She called the police.

contacts.what_was_asked: act on the break-ins and stalking
contacts.what_institution_did: Ran him in the system, found his real name and record, scanned the notes, questioned her several times, found the phone tracker and tested her car; did not arrest him.
contacts.quote: So I end up calling the cops, the cops come, and I tell them what's going on. They look him up in the system, and I give them his name, and they're like, ah, that can't be it.
contacts.what_happened_next: He disappeared; he was never caught.
contacts.notes: 'the cops figured out that he was tracking my phone' (28:59).

contacts.what_institution_did: Refused; under Texas rules she needs another in-person encounter with him.
contacts.quote: But the only way I can get a restraining order, even to this day, is if [perpetrator] is in the same room as me, or I see him personally, and he's like in the same space as me.
contacts.what_happened_next: No order.
contacts.notes: 'I asked for a restraining order and I was not allowed to get one. I tried multiple ways.'

contacts.what_was_asked: support and help with a restraining order
contacts.what_institution_did: Gave counseling and safety education, tried to get her a restraining order, and asked her to document red flags.
contacts.quote: but after going through victim service counseling, moving a couple of times to a very secure apartment now, I actually do feel safer.
contacts.what_happened_next: She feels safer.
contacts.notes: 'Victim services tried to get it for me as well' (28:59).

contacts.when: after she learned he was a con man
contacts.what_was_asked: warn the church and get support
contacts.what_institution_did: Did not care and gave no support.
contacts.quote: People would tell me that he came to the church, looking for me when I told the church exactly what had happened, and that he was a con man, like, oh, I better tell the church this. They didn't care, no one surrounded me.
contacts.what_happened_next: She turned away from organized religion.
contacts.notes: Earlier her small group 'ignored it' (E8 @ 32:22).

contacts.what_institution_did: Was supportive.
contacts.quote: Shout out to my work. They were very sweet.
contacts.what_happened_next: N/A

contacts.what_institution_did: He was told to leave.
contacts.quote: [perpetrator] ended up not seeing my brother, but he was told to leave. He left the church, but he's still out there.
contacts.what_happened_next: She reported it to police.

contacts.what_institution_did: No step shown.
contacts.quote: I even reported it to the cops that he showed up at my church for Easter.
contacts.what_happened_next: He is still at large.

persons.outcome_quote: And yeah, the cops weren't able to do anything. They weren't necessarily helpful.

coder_notes: Season 13 is an anthology of 22 episodes (E1-E22) covering 14 survivor stories. All 12 chunk files were read to their stated last lines; usage-limit interruptions meant resuming from notes, and no part was skipped. Coding choices: (1) Where a conviction or sentence happened but the survivor described it as too lenient (Amelia, Whitney, Grace), the court contact is coded acted_partly, and the note says the conviction itself was action. (2) Contacts where the harm was never disclosed (Zoe's school therapists, inpatient stay and doctor; Ruksana's AA) are not counted as contacts. (3) When harm ended through the person leaving or other non-institutional means and a sanction came later (Riley, Arya), the outcome is not_protected, per the instructions. (4) Perpetrator names were replaced with [perpetrator] in every quotation; other non-victims' names were avoided by choosing quotations that do not contain them. The task framing said 'institutions usually fail victims'. I did not let that steer the coding and coded only what the transcripts show; several institutions acted well (Natalia's hotline and court, Whitney's FBI, Grace's FBI). Uncertain items: Iris's case (the institutions dealt with the runaway, not the catfishing); Madison (the church saw boundary concerns but no harm was reported); Whitney's decisive worker (publicity-driven tip vs FBI).
